description: issue #837 (maintainer ruling #833): with `sprites` active, binding `tell`/`ask`/`each` as a VARIABLE is ACCEPTED. spec/grammar.md:390 makes every binding form accept any name -- including a keyword, a primitive, or an alias spelling of one -- as a normative MUST, so the three surface forms here (assignment's colon-place `:tell = 1`, its bare-place spelling `set ask to 2`, and a `for ... in` binder) all check clean. What a profile decides is whether a name WORKS, never whether a program may declare it (spec/grammar.md:412), and a binding declares nothing. The procedure and struct-constructor cases raise -- see reserved-procedures-with-sprites and reserved-struct-with-sprites, which are the declaration slots. Paired with reserved-bindings-without-sprites: both are clean, which is the point -- binding freedom is profile-independent. `"check": true` (semantic-checker only) -- no sprite is created and no events are produced.
